Guide to email marketing for nonprofits: Tips & examples
28 min
Updated:
Irek KlimczakIrek Klimczak
 Email marketing
 Newsletters
Share
Email marketing is one of the most cost-effective ways for nonprofits to build relationships, spread awareness, and turn supporters into donors — reaching almost everyone (most people have an email address), at low cost, with measurable results and a strong return on investment.
Produced with nonprofit tech consultants at TechSoup, this guide covers why email marketing matters for nonprofits, the best practices that work, inspiring real examples, a 10-step strategy for getting started, and the 5 core email types every nonprofit should send.
Why is email marketing crucial for nonprofits?
Let’s start by reviewing the reasons why email marketing is valuable for nonprofits.
|  |  |
 --- |
| Reason | Why it matters |
| Nearly everyone has email | Universal, cheap, accessible channel worldwide |
| Email is personal | Segment and personalize to boost engagement and donations |
| Cost-effective | Pay only for the software (priced by list size); send volume doesn’t raise cost; nonprofits get a 50% discount with GetResponse |
| High ROI | DMA reports an average email ROI of 38:1 |
| Measurable results | Track opens, clicks, conversion rates, and revenue |
Editor’s note
This article is a content collaboration between marketing experts at GetResponse – an email marketing platform and nonprofit organization tech consultants at TechSoup – a nonprofit tech marketplace.
1. Most of us have an email address
Email is one of the most widely-used channels of communication worldwide. It became universal because it’s cheap and accessible – almost everyone who uses the Internet has an email account and sends emails.
Whether your target audience lives in Asia, Europe, Africa, or America, you can use email to communicate effectively.
2. Email is personal
Email marketing allows nonprofit organizations to engage with their audience in a more personal way.
Nonprofits can segment their email list based on audience interests or preferences, then send personalized and targeted email campaigns that resonate with them.
Personalized emails with relevant content and calls to action can increase engagement and drive donations and other forms of support.
3. Email marketing is cost-effective
Most marketing channels are pay-per-click. Even if you’ve built an engaged audience on Facebook, the platform will limit your organic reach and force you to keep spending money on ads. This isn’t the case with email marketing.
If you’ve received someone’s permission to contact them via email, you’re almost guaranteed to reach their inbox, provided you follow standard email marketing best practices.
As a result, the only thing you need to pay for to run email campaigns is your email marketing service. Their price is usually based on the size of your email list, and the software comes with various built-in tools that’ll help you get your campaigns off the ground in moments.

Also, the number of emails you send does not impact the cost. This way, you can focus on building your list with people likely to become regular donors and run multiple campaigns to achieve that goal.

4. Email provides a high return on investment
According to a recent study by DMA, the average email ROI is 38:1. For every dollar you invest in email marketing, you can expect 38 dollars in return. That makes a great email marketing strategy so essential because it can help you get maximum ROI from your limited resources.
And if you regularly run A/B tests on your emails, you can generate an even more impressive return on your investment.
That means you won’t have to worry about the price of email marketing software. Instead, you can calculate the return on investment from the tools included in your plan, e.g., webinars, nonprofit landing pages, and automated emails.
5. Measurable results
Email marketing is a highly measurable marketing channel.
Most email marketing platforms provide nonprofits with critical data about their campaigns’ performance in their analytics dashboards. This includes metrics such as opens, clicks, conversion rates, and sales revenue.

Email marketing best practices for nonprofits and why they work
Below, you’ll find tried and tested ways to use emails and email series to turn contacts (your email readers) into regular donors. These ideas will help you tick off the most important aspects of email marketing for nonprofit organizations. Once you start, you can benchmark your email results against your previous campaigns and industry standards.
|  |  |
 --- |
| Best practice | Core idea |
| Create newsletter templates | Consistent branding + reusable design saves time |
| Automate communication | Behavior-based automation delivers personalized experiences (Learn → Like → Trust → Donate) |
| Monitor deliverability | Protect sender reputation; use a trusted platform, clean lists, SPF/DKIM/DMARC |
| Observe results | Track open, click-through, conversion, and unsubscribe rates |
| Find bottlenecks & improve | Address slow list growth and low open/click/conversion rates |
1. Create newsletter templates
A well-designed newsletter template is extremely important for email marketing success. First, it allows you to establish and maintain consistency in your organization’s branding and messaging. This helps build trust and recognition among your stakeholders.
Besides this, newsletter templates let you reuse designs for multiple email campaigns, streamlining the email creation process and saving you time and resources.
The efficiency a template offers is invaluable for nonprofits considering most operate with limited resources.
Here’s a case study with TechSoup Polska that proves just how important newsletter templates are: a 1200% increase in order value from a newsletter over a year.
Take a look at the rules that TechSoup Polska follows while creating their newsletters:
Structure. We divide our content into sections to facilitate information comprehension.
Consistency. We always use brand colors and utilize similar graphic elements.
Clarity. We strive to keep our newsletters clean and not overloaded with content.
Adjusting messages to the target group. We direct specific content to selected recipient groups (e.g., we inform users of Google for Nonprofits about Google Ad Grants training).
Here are a few pieces of advice from Liza Nema, Project Coordinator at TechSoup Polska, on how to prepare a professional newsletter template:
 Think about what kind of content you’ll be sending to your recipients.
 Choose a template.
 Customize the template according to your needs – use an email editor to change the colors and add logos and other graphic elements to align the design with your brand identity.
 Add a call-to-action so your recipients can perform the desired action: donate money, sign up for an event, etc.
 Before sending your newsletter, check its preview for desktop and mobile devices. Make sure your campaigns both look and work great.
 Analyze statistics and modify your content based on that data. Check your best-performing campaigns and choose a benchmark email for further campaigns.
 Don’t be afraid to experiment. It’s good to refresh your templates every now and then but remember to maintain your fundamental brand graphic elements.

2. Automate email marketing communication
Once your newsletter template is ready, you can start automating your communication. The goal is to use automation to build relationships with the people on your contact list and help them make the right decisions.
You can automate your email marketing communication accurately using customer data stored in your account.
Then with that, you can:
 Create automation events based on users’ behavior
 Take action based on selected conditions
 Use filters for even more precise targeting
 etc.

Automation will help you save time and resources for other projects.

3. Monitor your email deliverability
Email deliverability is one of the most important aspects of email marketing. You can’t reach your email campaign’s objective if your messages keep bouncing or getting moved to spam folders.
Therefore, you must constantly monitor and improve your email deliverability rate.
Here’s a formula you can use to calculate your deliverability rate.
[(# of emails delivered to the inbox/tabs/folders (excl.spam folder))/(# of sent emails – # of emails that generated a bounce)] \ 100%
With higher deliverability, your nonprofit organization has a better chance of engaging your email list and fostering meaningful connections.
Your deliverability rate also affects your email sender reputation. A high deliverability rate will help you preserve your nonprofit’s credibility and trustworthiness with mailbox providers.
To boost your email deliverability, ensure you choose a trusted email marketing platform with a great email deliverability reputation. Such providers have established relationships with internet service providers (ISPs) and clients, raising the chances of your email being delivered and staying out of the spam folder. For instance, GetResponse has a 99% overall email deliverability rate.
Also, regularly clean your email list to remove invalid or inactive email addresses, and implement email authentication protocols to help ISPs recognize your emails as legitimate.
Some of these protocols include SPF (Sender Policy Framework), DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail), and DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance).
4. Observe the results of your email marketing campaigns
Multiple factors contribute to effective email marketing communication. You must pay attention to your online marketing statistics and use data to make better decisions.
When it comes to individual emails, pay attention to engagement – a measure of how people interact with your emails. The most popular engagement metrics are:
 Open Rate: the percentage of contacts opening a specific email out of your total subscribers.
 Click-through rate: the percentage of contacts who clicked on a hyperlink, CTA, or image within a particular email.
 Conversion rate: the percentage of contacts who complete a goal expressed by the call to action.
 Unsubscribe rate: the percentage of contacts who have opted out from the mailing list after an email campaign.
Engagement is also critical to email deliverability. ISPs often consider recipient engagement when determining email placement. Therefore, the higher your recipient engagement level, the higher the chances of your email being delivered.
Check out GetResponse’s Email Marketing Benchmarks report if you’d like to compare your results against industry benchmarks.  The report offers loads of useful insights into emails, marketing automation, landing pages, and webinars.
5. Find bottlenecks and improve email marketing performance
It’s not possible to create a perfect email marketing program or campaign right out of the box. There’s always room for improvement. That’s why you’ll see some great, average, and rather poor results in your career. And it’s perfectly OK as long as you keep learning from your experience and continue testing new ideas.
The most common issues you observe at the beginning are;
Slow email list growth: Building a list organically takes time. But it doesn’t mean that you should sit and wait. You can do various things to speed up the list-building process. You can:
 Add a pop-up form to your website: Pop-up forms are hard to miss, and if you explain why joining your email list is a good idea, you can expect a high conversion rate.
 Run a competition: Competition can be both a sign-up incentive and an idea to engage with your audience.
 Write a blog post: Write about your organization, highlighting one of your key projects. Then, add a sign-up form or a link to your sign-up page from the blog post.
 Add an opt-in link to your email signature: I’m sure you send many emails every month. Make sure your recipients know they can sign-up for a newsletter.
 Find partnerships: Find people and organizations with a similar target audience and offer them guest posts and joint email campaigns. A strong network of partnerships is incredibly valuable.
 Run a webinar: Webinars are a great way to build a solid contact list. Do the research and choose an interesting topic for your target audience. Run promotional campaigns and invite people to register. Webinars are also perfect for content partnerships—team up with other organizations to get in front of their audience.
Here are some additional reads to help you learn how to build an email list from scratch and how to create a popup in moments.
The following three KPIs might relate to contact engagement. The key to a high engagement rate is relevance. That’s why segmentation is so important. If you group contacts based on their information needs and preferences, you’ll be able to plan and send communication they will engage with.
Low open rate. People are likely to open emails with the information they find valuable. Make sure that the three elements visible in the inbox before opening an email represent the contents of the message. The three elements are:
 Sender: Ensure people know the email comes from a reputable sender – you.
 Subject line: Spark interest, draw attention but refer to the contents of the email.
 Preheader: Use this extra space to explain or expand on the subject line.
Low click-through rate. Make sure your emails are mobile-friendly. Your call to action should be clear and easy to follow. You can run A/B tests to determine what content and messaging engages your audience most.
Low conversion rate. If you notice people open your emails and click the provided links but don’t do the action you were hoping for (e.g., don’t register for live events, don’t donate), take a step back and look carefully at your value proposition and audience.
In summary, clearly explain the goals of your organization and the ways you’re going to achieve them. Then put your message in front of the right crowd – look for people likely to support your fundraising campaigns. Send the right message to the right people and simplify the donation process, making it quick and easy.
Note: You’ll also want to ensure your email list is hygienic and well-maintained. To learn more about this, read our email list management guide.
Inspiring examples of nonprofit emails
There’s no better source of inspiration than a great email from your industry. And boy, are there many great emails sent by nonprofit organizations!
Once again, we teamed up with Liza to show you a few inspiring examples from our inboxes:
Nonprofit email marketing example 1: Kiva
An email from Kiva.
An email with a brief summary of 2020 and inviting supporters to start 2021 strong
What is this email campaign about?
Kiva is a nonprofit organization that lets you easily loan money to people that cannot get a loan from a bank.
This campaign provides a summary of their campaigns in 2020, highlighting how many people supported them, how much money they’ve donated, and how many loans they’ve made.
What’s so good about this email campaign?
After getting the recipients excited about how much impact they’re making, the email leads you to a single CTA, letting you lend money immediately.
This amazing tactic can help nonprofit organizations engage their audience better and gather more donations from their supporters.
Nonprofit email marketing example 2: Kiva
A fundraising email.
An email featuring the loans nearing the end of their fundraising period
What is this email campaign about?
This email campaign tells the story of one of many people whose life changed after they received a loan from Kiva.
What’s so go about this email campaign?
Sometimes it’s hard to get donors engaged in your cause. What can help is sharing a relatable story that shows the real impact a single donation can make.
In this email campaign, Kiva not only shows an example of a person whose life changed after they received a loan but also suggests which loans are about to expire.
This great tactic can drive fast responses from people who may otherwise hesitate to take action.
Nonprofit email marketing example 3: Movember
Movember email raising awareness.
An email sharing the mission and progress the Movember foundation made so far before the World Cancer Day
What is this email campaign about?
Movember is the leading charity changing the face of men’s health globally. It focuses on mental health and suicide prevention, prostate cancer, and testicular cancer.
This email campaign shares the mission and progresses the Movember Foundation made so far before World Cancer Day.
What’s so go about this email campaign?
With this email, Movember drives awareness among people who might not otherwise know the brand’s mission. What’s worth noting is that they’re doing this around World Cancer Day, which takes place in February rather than November, that’s typically associated with the charity.
Nonprofit email marketing example 4: Movember
An email with research and health projects funded by donors.
An email showing groundbreaking research and health projects funded by donors
What is this email campaign about?
This email shows a summary of all the groundbreaking research and health projects that were funded by people supporting the Movember cause.
What’s so go about this email campaign?
There’s no better way to engage your supporters and donors than to show them they’re making a real impact by joining your cause. This email does it so well. Not only is it informative, but also very well-designed.
In addition, the email ends with one primary CTA – make a $50 donation – that’s hard to miss or ignore.

What is email marketing?
Email marketing is the practice of sending targeted email messages (promotions, newsletters, product updates, or transactional confirmations) to subscribers who have willingly shared their contact information. Its goal is to build relationships and drive conversions through a channel you own and control.
Why is email marketing valuable for brands?
Email marketing delivers value through nine reinforcing strengths: a high ROI, an owned communication channel, hyper-targeted segmentation, automated nurturing at scale, boosted conversion rates, ecommerce sales, cross-channel support, stronger brand credibility, and deep performance insights. Together these make it one of the most measurable and cost-effective channels in digital marketing.
The traditional practice of sending email blasts to broad lists is no longer effective; businesses need to personalize the experience for each recipient, no matter where they are in the customer journey.
Dedicated email marketing services enhance relationship-building with potential and existing customers, which contributes directly to the company’s growth.
Here are in detail the key advantages that underscore the effectiveness of email marketing for businesses:
High return on investment (ROI)
Year after year, studies from industry analysts confirm email marketing’s impressive ROI. According to some estimates, brands can expect to see an average return of up to $36 for every $1 spent. This outperforms many other digital channels, including social ads, and underscores the significance of building strong, consistent communication with a well-maintained email list.
By targeting leads with precisely the right message at the right moment, you boost conversions while reducing wasted ad spend and broad-reaching campaigns that fail to resonate.
Owned communication channel
Unlike social media platforms, where algorithms can shift and cause sudden visibility declines, email lists are assets you own and provide a direct line of communication with your audience. You have full control over the way you contact your subscribers, free from external algorithmic changes.
This level of autonomy offers stability and predictability, so if you develop a loyal base of engaged subscribers, you can consistently reach them with minimal risk. A business that invests in building relationships through email has much more resilience when external platforms or paid advertising guidelines change.
Hyper-targeted audience segmentation
Modern email marketing platforms provide advanced segmentation tools that allow you to group your audience by demographics, behaviors, interests, purchase history, and more. Rather than blasting generic messages, you can deliver relevant content tailored to each subscriber’s needs.
Hyper-targeted segmentation leads to higher open rates, click-through rates, and conversion rates. Not only will your subscribers see an increase in the value and relevance of your messages, but you will also garner more trust and loyalty by continually sending them the content they want.
Automated nurturing at scale
An effective email marketing strategy doesn’t rely on manual sending of individual messages. Instead, you build automated workflows that trigger emails based on specific user actions or milestones. This could be a welcome series for new subscribers, follow-ups for those who clicked on a particular link, or re-engagement sequences for dormant subscribers.
Dedicated email marketing platforms like GetResponse allow you to create powerful, visual automation workflows that run around the clock. These workflows help you nurture leads and customers at scale without constant oversight. By automating these touchpoints, you ensure every subscriber receives consistent, timely communication tailored to their stage in the buyer’s journey.
Boosted conversion rates
Email marketing is highly effective at converting prospects into paying customers. This is because the recipient is often in a focused state when they receive these messages, such as when checking their inbox at work or during downtime, which leads to a higher level of engagement.
Thoughtful subject lines, compelling copy, and strong calls-to-action guide subscribers toward a specific goal, whether it’s purchasing a product or signing up for an event. With personalization, segmented lists, and AI-driven optimizations, the likelihood of conversion increases even further.
Drives ecommerce sales
Ecommerce businesses greatly benefit from email marketing in driving product awareness, announcing sales, and recovering lost revenue from cart abandonments. Features such as abandoned cart emails and AI-driven product recommendations have proven especially powerful, leading to direct increases in sales by encouraging would-be customers to complete their purchases.
Integrations with platforms like Shopify, WooCommerce, and other ecommerce systems enable them to automate personalized messages that highlight products based on each subscriber’s browsing or purchase history.
Supports cross-channel campaigns
Email works beautifully alongside other digital channels, such as social media, paid ads, and content marketing, by combining them into cohesive cross-channel campaigns. For instance, you might promote a webinar on social media but use an email follow-up to deliver the replay and gather additional data.
With a single platform like GetResponse, you can unify your marketing messages across email, SMS, web push, and more. This holistic approach ensures that your audience receives consistent communication wherever they interact with your brand, increasing overall impact.
Enhances brand credibility and authority
Consistently delivering valuable insights, news, and offers via email builds trust and positions you as an authority in your field.
Over time, your subscribers will associate your brand with valuable content, which will enhance your credibility. This can help you get repeat purchases, positive reviews, referrals, and long-term customer loyalty, all of which are great for any business that wants sustainable growth.
Provides deep performance insights
Every aspect of an email campaign can be measured and analyzed, from open rates and click-through rates (CTR) to conversions and revenue generated. Marketers can quickly see what’s working and what isn’t and then optimize accordingly.
Modern platforms offer real-time analytics, intuitive dashboards, and automation performance reports that let you pinpoint high-performing campaigns to design future campaigns and weed out underperformers.
How email marketing has changed in 2026?
Email marketing in 2026 is defined by three shifts: deeper personalization, AI-assisted content generation, and privacy-first strategies. Marketers now tailor messages more precisely, use AI to create and optimize copy faster, and design campaigns around data protection and reduced reliance on traditional tracking.
More personalization
Personalization in email marketing strategies is no longer limited to simply inserting a recipient’s name in a predefined template; brands now leverage vast amounts of data to deliver tailored content to deliver real value in every communication. Marketers segment their audiences based on a variety of factors, including purchase history, browsing behaviors, and engagement levels, and create messages that resonate on a deeper level. This move toward hyper-personalization has enhanced the user experience and boosted engagement rates.
Incorporating dynamic content also greatly improves personalization efforts. Retailers can create emails with products or offers targeted to audience segments that are delivered in real time. For example, a retailer might showcase different offers based on a user’s past purchases or browsing history, enhancing the likelihood of conversion.
AI content generation
There are more brands now that are increasingly using AI-driven tools to generate subject lines, body copy, and personalized recommendations with unprecedented efficiency. These tools analyze user data to identify trends and preferences, allowing marketers to create highly relevant and engaging content tailored to individual subscribers.
AI enables continuous optimization through automated testing and data analysis. For instance, AI algorithms can evaluate the performance of various email elements, such as subject lines and calls to action, to determine which resonates best with specific audience segments. This data-driven approach allows brands to refine their messaging in real time, ensuring that each email is targeted and compelling enough to drive engagement.
Privacy-first strategies
With growing concerns over data privacy and consumers becoming increasingly conscious of how their personal data is used, brands are adopting privacy-first strategies that prioritize transparency and ethical practices. They are compelled to establish clear communication about data collection and usage and must comply with regulations such as GDPR and CCPA.
Privacy-first strategies encourage businesses to adopt consent-based marketing approaches. Instead of focusing solely on list size, brands are now prioritizing the quality of their subscriber lists. By promoting double opt-in processes and providing clear value propositions for subscribing, businesses can ensure that their email lists consist of engaged individuals who are genuinely interested in their content. This leads to higher open and click-through rates and also establishes trust for long-term customer relationships.

How do you build an email marketing strategy from scratch?
To build an email marketing strategy from scratch, align email with your overall marketing goals, set measurable goals, choose the right KPIs, identify your target audience, segment your lists effectively, and create compelling offers or lead magnets. Working through these steps in order gives your campaigns a clear purpose and a way to measure success.
Below, I’ll describe in detail the core steps to guide you from an empty subscriber list to a flourishing, conversion-driven program.
| Step | Action | What to do |
 --- 
| 1 | Align email with your overall marketing strategy | Tie email content to broader goals; keep messaging consistent across channels |
| 2 | Set measurable goals | Define success (engagement, conversion, retention) and quantify it |
| 3 | Choose the right KPIs | Track open rate, CTR, ROI, unsubscribe rate (and revenue attribution) |
| 4 | Identify your target audience | Build buyer personas from analytics, feedback, and behavior |
| 5 | Segment lists effectively | Group by demographics, purchase history, engagement, interests |
| 6 | Create compelling offers or lead magnets | Use ebooks, webinars, discounts, gated content to capture sign-ups |
1. Align email with your overall marketing strategy
Email marketing should never exist in a vacuum. Instead, integrate it into your broader marketing objectives.
If your primary goal is to increase awareness of a new product line, shape your email content around product education, trial invitations, or special offers. If you want to drive more webinar attendees or grow a membership community, craft an email series promoting these upcoming events and highlighting the benefits of joining. Make sure that messaging is consistent across your website, social channels, and email campaigns.
2. Set measurable goals
Establishing clear, measurable goals is essential for tracking your email marketing performance. Goals range from increasing engagement rates, boosting conversion rates, or improving customer retention. By defining what success looks like, you can create targeted campaigns that measure progress against these objectives.
For example, aims such as improving engagement could be quantified by increasing open rates or click-through rates (CTR), while conversion goals might focus on measuring the number of subscribers who complete a purchase after receiving a specific email campaign. Regularly evaluating your goals can help you fine-tune your approach and optimize performance.
3. Choose the right KPIs
To effectively measure the success of your email marketing efforts, it’s crucial to identify and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs). Common KPIs for email marketing include the following:
 Open rate: This measures the percentage of recipients who opened your email, indicating the effectiveness of your subject line and preheader text in attracting attention.
 Click-through rate (CTR): The CTR, which measures the percentage of recipients who click on one or more links within your email, offers insights into the relevance and appeal of your content.
 Return on investment (ROI): Calculating the ROI of your email campaigns helps assess the financial effectiveness of your strategy. Tracking income generated from campaigns relative to costs incurred provides valuable insights into profitability. To get the revenue side right, you need to know which emails actually drove purchases – tools like the GetResponse’s Revenue Attribution tracks this automatically across all your message types.
 Unsubscribe rate: This metric indicates the percentage of subscribers who opted out of receiving future emails. Monitoring this can help identify issues with content relevance or frequency, enabling you to make necessary adjustments.
4. Identify your target audience
Understanding your target audience is fundamental to crafting effective email campaigns. Begin by developing detailed buyer personas that encapsulate your ideal customers’ demographics, preferences, pain points, and behaviors.
Gather data from customer interactions across various touchpoints, such as website analytics, customer feedback, and social media engagement. This comprehensive understanding enables you to tailor content that not only resonates but also feels personal and relevant to each subscriber.
5. Segmenting lists effectively
Once you’ve identified your target audience, the effective segmentation of your email lists is essential. Segmenting allows you to group subscribers based on common characteristics or behaviors, such as demographics, purchase history, engagement levels, and interests. By sending tailored content to these specific segments, you can enhance the relevance of your communication.
For example, offering exclusive discounts to lapsed customers or sending product recommendations based on past purchases can significantly improve engagement and conversion rates.
Leveraging GetResponse’s powerful segmentation tools enables you to efficiently categorize and manage your subscriber lists, ensuring that each audience group receives targeted messaging that resonates with their unique preferences.
6. Create compelling offers or lead magnets
To grow your email list and capture interested subscribers, consider creating compelling offers or lead magnets. These valuable resources can include ebooks, whitepapers, webinars, discount codes, or exclusive content that addresses specific problems or interests of your target audience. Effective lead magnets provide a clear value proposition for subscriptions, enticing visitors to share their email addresses in exchange for valuable content.
